Apple Black Rot.description: Black rot is a fungal disease of apple caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa. It produces circular brown spots on leaves and dark brown rotting lesions on fruit, often with visible pycnidia (black dots) in the center.
Apple Black Rot.cause: Fungal disease caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa.
Apple Black Rot.symptoms: Circular brown leaf spots with purple margins, dark brown rotting lesions on fruit with concentric rings.
Apple Black Rot.treatment: Remove mummified fruit and cankered branches. Apply fungicide during the growing season.
Apple Black Rot.prevention: Prune dead wood, remove fallen leaves, and apply dormant sprays before bud break.
Apple Black Rot.disclaimer: This is general guidance only. Consult an agricultural expert before treatment.

Apple Cedar Rust.description: Cedar rust is a fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. It requires both apple and cedar/juniper hosts. It produces bright orange-yellow spots on apple leaves and deformed fruit.
Apple Cedar Rust.cause: Fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae (requires cedar alternate host).
Apple Cedar Rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces, horn-like tubes on leaf undersides, deformed fruit.
Apple Cedar Rust.treatment: Apply fungicide at pink bud stage. Remove nearby cedar trees if possible.
Apple Cedar Rust.prevention: Remove juniper/cedar alternate hosts within 2 miles. Plant resistant apple varieties.
Apple Cedar Rust.disclaimer: This is general guidance only. Consult an agricultural expert before treatment.

Tomato Target Spot.description: Target spot is a fungal disease of tomato caused by Corynespora cassiicola. It produces brown spots with concentric rings on leaves, stems, and fruit, leading to defoliation and fruit rot.
Tomato Target Spot.cause: Fungal disease caused by Corynespora cassiicola.
Tomato Target Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on leaves, stems, and fruit. Premature leaf drop.
Tomato Target Spot.treatment: Apply fungicide (azoxystrobin or difenoconazole-based). Remove infected debris.
Tomato Target Spot.prevention: Practice crop rotation, improve air circulation, and avoid overhead irrigation.
Tomato Target Spot.disclaimer: This is general guidance only. Consult an agricultural expert before treatment.

Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.description: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) is a geminivirus spread by whiteflies. It causes upward leaf curling, yellowing, stunting, and significant fruit yield loss.
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.cause: Viral disease caused by Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV), spread by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.symptoms: Upward leaf curling, yellowing of leaf margins, stunted growth, reduced fruit set.
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.treatment: No cure. Remove and destroy infected plants. Control whitefly populations.
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties, install yellow sticky traps, and control whitefly vectors.
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.disclaimer: This is general guidance only. Consult an agricultural expert before treatment.
